**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require real authorization before executing imports**

Because this route is registered directly in `buildApp` and `main` serves `app.fetch` without an auth middleware, any caller who can reach the resident server can set `x-confirm-import: yes` and pass arbitrary `owner`/`repo` query values to run GitHub writes with the server token. The header is not a secret or tied to a user/profile, so this bypasses the existing token/secret pattern used by callback/confirm routes; require an authenticated and authorized actor before calling `executeXlsxImport`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resolve milestone titles before creating issues**

When an issue row includes a milestone name from the template, such as `v1`, this passes that string directly to GitHub's create-issue payload. GitHub associates issues by milestone number, and the importer neither resolves the title nor uses the number returned by `createMilestone`, so imports that include milestone titles fail to associate or can return 422; resolve names to numbers before issue creation or make the column explicitly numeric.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use field_type when setting Project v2 values**

Rows carry `field_type`, but this mutation always sends `value: { text: $value }` and the `fieldType` variable is never referenced. In contexts importing date, number, single-select, or iteration Project v2 fields, GitHub expects the corresponding value member, so those rows fail even though the parser/template accept `field_type`; either restrict validation to text fields or branch on `fieldType` when building the mutation value.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
